observations: MATERIALS.json contains 12 assets, each an ordered list of 10 [x,y] pairs in a 0-100 coordinate space. a01-a03 are closed 10-point ring outlines of increasing size; a04-a06 are staircase-like polylines (a06 is a near-vertical mirror of a04/a05); a07-a09 are zigzag polylines spanning nearly the full width; a10-a12 are gently arcing near-diagonal curves. INPUT.json supplies 8 directed connections forming four 3-asset chains: a01->a02->a03, a04->a05->a06, a07->a08->a09, a10->a11->a12.
interpretation: Within each connection chain the three point lists are geometric kin: same point count, similar shape, progressive offsets. I treated each chain as a short morph lineage and rendered the three supplied assets solid, with point-index-wise interpolated outlines filling the gaps between consecutive chained assets.
new_relation_or_transformation: Linear point-index-wise interpolation (6 intermediate steps per pair, chained a->b->c) rescaled from the 0-100 input space into four 720x480 panels; source assets drawn solid with coordinate dots, interpolations dashed with opacity peaking mid-transition.
possible_dependence_on_input: The trace is fully derived from the supplied coordinates and connection lists; positions, shapes, chain grouping, and panel labels come directly from MATERIALS.json and INPUT.json. No external data was added.
limitations: Interpolation assumes the k-th point of one asset corresponds to the k-th point of the next, which the data does not state. Connections were used only as grouping hints; no causal or semantic relationship between assets is demonstrated. Rendering choices (step count, opacity, colors) are mine.
